seo.title: Allen, TX Home Appraisals | American Appraisal Alliance
seo.description: Allen, TX home appraisals grounded in the city's neighborhood records: plat eras, housing types, subdivision phases and Downtown District rules.

mainEntity.name: My Allen subdivision was platted in phases. Does that matter for comparables?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can. Phases of the same subdivision may differ in lot sizes, builders, floor plans or amenities, and later phases can be years newer than earlier ones. The appraiser identifies the subject’s phase and plat, then favors sales from the same phase or from phases that are genuinely similar.

mainEntity.name: Is every 75002 or 75013 address inside the City of Allen?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Nearly all City of Allen addresses use one of those two ZIP codes, but ZIP codes are delivery areas, not city limits. The city’s own address map includes a small number of 75002 addresses coded to neighboring communities, and Allen also has an extraterritorial jurisdiction outside its limits. The appraiser confirms jurisdiction from parcel and boundary records.

mainEntity.name: Does a creek or greenbelt behind my Allen home affect the appraisal?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is examined, not assumed. Allen’s creek corridors, including Cottonwood, Rowlett and Watters creeks, can bring open views and also flood-zone and drainage considerations. The appraiser checks the property’s flood-zone status and looks for comparable sales with similar exposure before making any adjustment.

mainEntity.name: How does the Downtown District affect older property near downtown Allen?

acceptedAnswer.text: In 2023 the city replaced its Central Business District zoning with a Downtown District and created a Downtown Design Review Board that oversees modifications within the district. If a property lies inside that district, its zoning and any review requirements are part of what the appraiser verifies; planned downtown projects are considered only as far as the market already reflects them.

seo.title: Celina, TX Home Appraisals | American Appraisal Alliance
seo.description: Celina, TX home appraisals for a market built mostly since 2010, with city-versus-ETJ, two-county and new-construction comparable issues addressed.

mainEntity.name: My address says Celina. Is the home inside the City of Celina?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Celina’s 2040 plan covers about 76 square miles that include the city, its extraterritorial jurisdiction and areas covered by boundary agreements, and some master-planned communities with Celina addresses lie in the ETJ. Whether a home is inside the city affects taxes, services and land-use rules, so the appraiser confirms it from boundary and parcel records.

mainEntity.name: How are comparables chosen when so many Celina homes are new?

acceptedAnswer.text: In a market built largely since 2010, recent resales and builder sales from the same or a similar subdivision are often the most relevant evidence. The appraiser looks closely at lot size, builder, upgrades and the terms of new-construction sales, rather than assuming a new home and a five-year-old resale are interchangeable.

mainEntity.name: Which county is my Celina property in?

acceptedAnswer.text: The City of Celina lies in both Collin and Denton counties according to the U.S. Census Bureau’s 2020 place-by-county records. The parcel record, not the mailing address, establishes the county and therefore the appraisal district that values the property for taxes.

seo.title: Frisco, TX Appraisal Services | American Appraisal Alliance
seo.description: Frisco, TX home appraisals that account for Collin vs. Denton County parcels, HOA and planned-development rules, and Rail District reinvestment.

mainEntity.name: Frisco spans two counties. Does that affect my appraisal?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can. Frisco lies in both Collin and Denton counties, and a Frisco mailing address does not tell you which one applies. The appraiser identifies the county from the parcel record, which matters most for property tax matters, where the appraisal district and its records follow the parcel’s county.

mainEntity.name: Is my HOA part of the appraisal?

acceptedAnswer.text: The HOA is part of the property’s market context. Dues, amenities and deed restrictions differ between Frisco communities, so the appraiser favors comparable sales from the same or a similar association and may ask you for the HOA name and governing documents.

mainEntity.name: Should I order an appraisal before protesting my Frisco property value?

acceptedAnswer.text: An independent appraisal can document market value as of a specific date and be offered as evidence in a protest. It is prepared impartially under USPAP; no appraiser can promise a particular value or protest outcome.

mainEntity.name: Does the Rail District reinvestment change values near downtown Frisco?

acceptedAnswer.text: Completed improvements are part of the neighborhood as it exists on the effective date, and their influence is measured through sales. Programs that are still being funded or built are not treated as completed features of the market.

seo.title: McKinney, TX Home Appraiser | American Appraisal Alliance
seo.description: USPAP-compliant McKinney, TX appraisals that verify historic designations, city limits and downtown redevelopment timelines. Request an appraisal.

mainEntity.name: Does a historic designation raise or lower a McKinney home’s value?

acceptedAnswer.text: Neither automatically. A designation can affect what an owner may change and may make the property eligible for certain programs. The appraiser treats the designation as a property characteristic, identifies it for the subject and the comparables, and lets local sales evidence show whether it matters.

mainEntity.name: How can I tell whether my McKinney home is in a historic district?

acceptedAnswer.text: The City of McKinney publishes historic district, overlay and incentive-zone maps through its historic preservation resources and GIS portal. Because McKinney uses several distinct designations, confirm the specific one that applies to your address rather than relying on a neighborhood description.

mainEntity.name: My address says McKinney. Is the property inside the city limits?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Postal addresses and municipal boundaries are different things. McKinney’s city-limit map is built from annexation ordinances, so the appraiser checks the parcel’s jurisdiction, which can affect taxes, zoning and the comparables that best fit the property.

mainEntity.name: Will downtown McKinney’s redevelopment plans be reflected in my appraisal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Adopted plans and scheduled infrastructure work are noted as market context, but the appraisal values the property as of its effective date. Planned work is not treated as completed, and any influence on value must be visible in market evidence.

seo.title: Plano, TX Home Appraisals | American Appraisal Alliance
seo.description: Independent, USPAP-compliant home appraisals in Plano, TX, informed by local preserves, heritage districts and rental rules. Request an appraisal.

mainEntity.name: Does living near Oak Point or Arbor Hills automatically raise a Plano home’s appraised value?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Proximity to a preserve, greenbelt or trail is a location characteristic the appraiser analyzes, not a fixed adjustment. Where the market shows a measurable difference, it is supported with comparable sales — ideally homes with and without similar open-space exposure. Where the evidence does not show a difference, none is made.

mainEntity.name: My home is in or near Historic Downtown Plano. What should the appraiser know?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell the appraiser whether the property is a designated heritage resource or lies within a heritage district, and share any records of approved exterior work. Plano’s heritage program can affect what owners may change, so the appraiser confirms the designation at the property level and looks for comparable homes with similar status rather than relying on a neighborhood name.

mainEntity.name: Can DART Silver Line service be factored into a Plano appraisal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only to the extent buyers and sellers have actually reacted to it. An appraisal reflects the market as of its effective date, so rail service or planned public projects are considered through observable sales evidence, not through assumptions about future demand.

mainEntity.name: I own a Plano rental property. Is an appraisal different for a rental?

acceptedAnswer.text: The appraisal still values the real property under the scope you request. For a rental, the appraiser may ask about lease terms, condition and any applicable city registration, and the intended use — such as an estate, divorce or financing matter — determines which approaches to value are appropriate.

seo.title: Prosper, TX Home Appraisals | American Appraisal Alliance
seo.description: Prosper, TX appraisals that confirm Collin or Denton County, weigh builder and resale evidence, and follow the town's plan and tollway guidelines.

mainEntity.name: Prosper is in two counties. Why does that matter for an appraisal?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Town of Prosper extends into both Collin and Denton counties. The county determines which appraisal district values the property for taxes and which public records apply, so it matters most for tax protests and for comparing homes on either side of the line.

mainEntity.name: Are homes along the Dallas North Tollway corridor treated differently?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not automatically. Prosper has adopted design guidelines for the tollway corridor as part of its comprehensive plan, and corridor location is a characteristic the appraiser describes. Any effect on value has to be shown by comparable sales, such as homes with similar exposure to the corridor.

mainEntity.name: Do new-construction sales count as comparables in Prosper?

acceptedAnswer.text: They can. With most of Prosper’s housing built since 2010, builder sales are part of the market. The appraiser verifies the sale terms, any incentives and the finished features, and weighs them against resales of similar homes.

seo.title: Addison, TX Appraisals | American Appraisal Alliance
seo.description: Addison, TX residential appraisals for a mostly multifamily market: condominium, townhome and detached-home comparables, compared like with like.

mainEntity.name: How are Addison condominiums and townhomes compared?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is compared primarily with other condominiums or townhomes — ideally in the same project or similar projects — because their buyers, ownership structure and association costs differ from detached homes. The appraiser also considers association dues, project characteristics and any limits on rentals or financing that affect the market.

mainEntity.name: Can sales in neighboring Dallas be used for an Addison home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, when Addison itself lacks recent similar sales. Because Addison is a separate town with its own taxes and services, the appraiser explains why any outside sale is a reasonable substitute and adjusts for the differences the market supports.

mainEntity.name: Does Addison Airport or the Silver Line affect home values?

acceptedAnswer.text: They are location characteristics to examine, not automatic adjustments. The appraiser describes the property’s setting and relies on sales evidence — for example, homes with and without similar exposure — before making any adjustment.

seo.title: North Dallas Home Appraisals | American Appraisal Alliance
seo.description: Home appraisals in northern Dallas that start with records: city limits, which of five counties applies, current zoning and conservation districts.

mainEntity.name: What exactly is North Dallas?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is a commonly used description for the northern part of the City of Dallas rather than an official municipality, and its edges are described differently by different people. For an appraisal, the meaningful facts are the property’s actual city, county, zoning and subdivision, which are confirmed from public records.

mainEntity.name: Can a Dallas address be outside Dallas County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the City of Dallas extends into Dallas, Collin, Denton, Kaufman and Rockwall counties. The county controls which appraisal district values the property and which records apply.

mainEntity.name: Does ForwardDallas change my property’s zoning?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The City of Dallas describes ForwardDallas 2.0, adopted in September 2024, as a land-use planning guide that does not rezone property. The appraiser relies on the property’s current zoning and any applicable conservation-district or planned-development ordinance.

seo.title: Richardson, TX Home Appraisals | American Appraisal Alliance
seo.description: Richardson, TX home appraisals by a Texas Certified Residential Appraiser, grounded in Silver Line, CityLine and Envision Richardson planning facts.

mainEntity.name: Does being near a Silver Line station affect a Richardson home’s value?

acceptedAnswer.text: Proximity to the CityLine/Bush or UT Dallas station is a location factor the appraiser can examine, but there is no automatic adjustment. Service began in October 2025, so any effect has to be demonstrated through sales that reflect buyers’ actual response.

mainEntity.name: What does the Envision Richardson plan mean for my appraisal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Envision Richardson is a policy framework adopted in November 2024. It signals where the city expects reinvestment, but a plan is not a completed project. The appraiser considers current zoning and existing conditions, and treats future change only as far as the market already reflects it.

mainEntity.name: Is my home part of CityLine or the Innovation Quarter?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are planning and development districts, not ZIP codes or neighborhoods in the residential sense. CityLine is divided into three separately zoned areas, and the Innovation Quarter is described by the city in general terms. The appraiser confirms how a specific parcel is zoned using Richardson’s interactive Zoning Atlas.

mainEntity.name: Which Richardson sales are comparable to my home?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best comparables share the subject’s market area, property type and setting. In Richardson that means paying attention to which side of a major corridor, district boundary or creek greenbelt a sale sits on, rather than simply measuring distance.

seo.description: American Appraisal Alliance appraisal service areas in Denton County, Texas.

seo.title: Aubrey, TX Property Appraisals | American Appraisal Alliance
seo.description: Aubrey, TX appraisals for subdivision homes and rural acreage, with the one-mile ETJ and Ray Roberts Lake flowage easements considered.

mainEntity.name: My Aubrey-area property is outside the city limits. Does that matter?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Aubrey maintains a one-mile extraterritorial jurisdiction where the city regulates the subdivision of land but not zoning. Properties in the ETJ and inside the city can differ in rules and services, so the appraiser confirms which applies before selecting comparables.

mainEntity.name: How are acreage or horse properties near Aubrey appraised?

acceptedAnswer.text: They are compared with sales of similar rural or acreage properties, with attention to land size, improvements such as barns and fencing, access and utilities. Subdivision homes on small lots are generally a different market and are not substituted without explanation.

mainEntity.name: What is a flowage easement near Ray Roberts Lake?

acceptedAnswer.text: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers describes a flowage easement as privately owned land on which the government holds the perpetual right to flood, with restrictions on what owners may do there. If a property is affected, the easement is part of the property rights being appraised.

seo.title: Carrollton, TX Home Appraisals | American Appraisal Alliance
seo.description: Carrollton, TX home appraisals across Dallas, Denton and Collin counties, focused on 1970s-era housing, renovations and finished square footage.

mainEntity.name: Which county is my Carrollton home in?

acceptedAnswer.text: Carrollton extends into Dallas, Denton and Collin counties. The parcel record establishes the county and the appraisal district that values the property for taxes, which is especially important for tax-protest appraisals.

mainEntity.name: How does the age of Carrollton’s housing affect an appraisal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Much of Carrollton was built during a 1970s growth period, and many homes have since been updated to very different degrees. The appraiser compares homes of similar era and pays close attention to the extent and quality of renovations, which often explain differences between otherwise similar sales.

mainEntity.name: Does being near a DART station change a Carrollton home’s value?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not automatically. Rail access is a location characteristic, and any influence must be shown by sales of comparable homes with similar proximity. The appraisal reflects the market as of its effective date.

seo.title: Lewisville, TX Home Appraisals | American Appraisal Alliance
seo.description: Lewisville, TX appraisals that separate detached, attached and condo markets and check lake flood zones and Corps of Engineers flowage easements.

mainEntity.name: Could my Lewisville property be affected by a lake flowage easement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properties near Lewisville Lake can be. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers describes flowage easements as private land on which the government holds the perpetual right to flood, with restrictions on use. If one applies, the appraiser identifies it and considers its effect on the property rights being valued.

mainEntity.name: Lewisville has many apartments and townhomes. How does that affect comparables?

acceptedAnswer.text: Each housing type is compared with its own kind. A detached home is compared with detached homes, and an attached or condominium unit with similar attached units, because the buyers and ownership costs differ.

mainEntity.name: Is all of Lewisville in Denton County?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. According to the U.S. Census Bureau, Lewisville extends into both Denton and Dallas counties. The parcel record determines the county and appraisal district.

seo.title: Little Elm, TX Home Appraisals | American Appraisal Alliance
seo.description: Little Elm, TX home appraisals that confirm current flood-map status, lake easements and rental registration before comparing lakeside sales.

@graph.name: Residential appraisal in Little Elm, Texas

mainEntity.name: My Little Elm home was outside the flood zone before 2011. Has that changed?

acceptedAnswer.text: It may have. The Town of Little Elm notes that FEMA revised the Denton County flood maps effective April 18, 2011, including base flood elevations for streams and Lake Lewisville. The appraiser reports the property’s current flood-zone designation from the effective map.

mainEntity.name: Does a rental home in Little Elm need anything special for an appraisal?

acceptedAnswer.text: The appraisal values the real property under the agreed scope. Little Elm requires non-owner-occupied homes to be registered annually as rental properties, so for a rental the appraiser may ask about leases, condition and registration as part of understanding the property.

mainEntity.name: Is a lake view automatically worth more in Little Elm?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Lake proximity is examined through comparable sales, together with flood-zone status, any flowage easement and the specific view and access the property has.

seo.title: The Colony, TX Home Appraisals | American Appraisal Alliance
seo.description: The Colony, TX appraisals organized by development era, from the 1970s planned community to newer subdivisions, with lakeshore checks.

@graph.name: Residential appraisal in The Colony, Texas

mainEntity.name: Why do The Colony’s oldest neighborhoods need different comparables?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Colony began as a single planned development in the 1970s and has added newer neighborhoods since. Homes from the original development era are best compared with each other, with careful attention to updates, while newer subdivisions form their own comparison sets.

mainEntity.name: Does living near Lewisville Lake change an appraisal in The Colony?

acceptedAnswer.text: Lake proximity is examined, not assumed. The appraiser checks flood-zone status and any U.S. Army Corps of Engineers flowage easement, and relies on sales of homes with similar lake exposure before making any adjustment.

mainEntity.name: Is The Colony in more than one county?

acceptedAnswer.text: According to the U.S. Census Bureau’s 2020 place-by-county records, The Colony lies within Denton County. The parcel record confirms the county for any individual property.
